context_requirements: Expression of calpain-1/calpain-2 (CAPN1/CAPN2) and their endogenous inhibitor calpastatin (CAST)
Functional p53 pathway for the p53-dependent G1 arrest/apoptosis arm
Active caspase machinery for apoptosis amplification
Cellular context where calpain activity contributes to turnover of p53 or other short-lived regulators
falsifiers: No change in CDKN1A or other p53 target genes at 6 or 24 h in any p53-wild-type line
No reduction in proliferation/cell-cycle genes at 24 h
Strong and selective upregulation of generic stress markers (HSPA1A, DNAJB1, HMOX1) without p53 or cell-cycle changes
Identical transcriptional response in p53-null and p53-wild-type lines

evidence.supports: Calpain inhibitor 1 increases activated p53 and p21 and induces p53-dependent G0/G1 arrest and apoptosis in tumor cell lines
Calpastatin, the endogenous calpain inhibitor, is cleaved by caspases during apoptosis, linking calpain inhibition to apoptotic regulation
Calpastatin cleavage occurs during apoptosis and is blocked by caspase inhibitors, supporting crosstalk between calpain and caspase pathways
Calpain inhibitor I can overcome TRAIL resistance and enhance caspase-8 and caspase-3 activation in colon cancer cells

changes: Removed PMID 15777753 from evidence: the abstract reports in vivo neuroprotection by a calpain inhibitor, not a transcriptional response, so it does not support the stated claim.
Kept PMID 10845425, 9705209, 9894609, and 15120327 because their abstracts directly support the stated claims about p53/p21 induction, calpastatin cleavage, and caspase activation.
No gene direction changes were made because the retrieved abstracts do not provide gene-level directionality for the listed landmark genes.
No specificity, line-response, kinetics, or magnitude changes were made because the retrieved abstracts do not contain the necessary cell-line or time-course data.
